region.text: Anjou and Maine: Robert the Strong's county and mission in 861

ledger.note: 861: Charles the Bald makes peace with Robert the Strong and appoints him Count of Anjou and margrave of Neustria, re-creating the Breton March. 'In 861, Charles made peace with Robert and appointed him Count of Anjou' (Robert the Strong page); 're-created the Breton March in 861 and appointed Robert the Strong margrave' (March page). The page gives lands as Anjou and Maine only.

region.text: western Anjou, recognised as part of Brittany by the Treaty of Entrammes (863)

ledger.note: 863: By the Treaty of Entrammes Charles the Bald recognises western Anjou as part of Brittany under Salomon. 'Charles negotiated the Treaty of Entrammes with Salomon, King of Brittany, recognizing western Anjou as part of Brittany.' The Robert the Strong page: Salomon made his peace in 863 after Robert hired the Seine Vikings against him in 862.

region.text: the Neustrian march between the Seine and the Loire: Ile-de-France, Orléanais and Touraine (a reading of 'the region between the Loire and the Seine, the ancient kingdom of Neustria')

ledger.note: 886: Charles the Fat gives Odo the title of margrave; the March page names no land. The land between the Seine and the Loire (Duchy page's Neustria) is bridged here at confidence 1 because no page dates the Robertians' acquisition of Paris, Orléans or Tours.

936: The title dux Francorum is revived for Hugh the Great, 'Between 936 and 943'; in 943 the king 'invested Hugh with the duchy of France' (Flodoard). The March of Neustria becomes the Duchy of Francia; same state, same colour.

ledger.note: 936: Hugh the Great holds 'nearly all the land between the Loire and the Seine, excluding Anjou'; the page does not say when Anjou left Robertian hands, so the loss is booked at the first year the page excludes it (confidence 1).

region.text: Laon, surrendered by Louis IV as the price of his release

ledger.note: 946: Hugh the Great releases the captured Louis IV on condition that he surrender Laon. Louis IV was captured by the Normans and handed to Hugh in 945 (in exchange for their young duke Richard), and in 946 Hugh released him on condition that he surrender Laon (page, closely paraphrased).

wars.name: Robert the Strong's war against Salomon and the Vikings

zones.text: western Anjou, recognised as part of Brittany by the Treaty of Entrammes (863)

wars.outcome: Robert hired the former Seine Vikings against Salomon in 862 ('6,000 pounds silver'); Salomon made his peace in 863 and western Anjou was recognised as Breton; Robert was killed at Brissarthe on 2 July 866 by Vikings under Hastein and Bretons under Salomon.
wars.note: Entrammes (863) is on the March page; the Robert page is silent on it.

wars.name: Hugh the Great and Louis IV

zones.text: Laon, surrendered by Louis IV as the price of his release

wars.outcome: Louis IV attacked Hugh's fortresses from 938; Louis was captured by the Normans and handed to Hugh in 945; Hugh freed him in 946 on condition he surrender Laon; Hugh was excommunicated at Ingelheim in 948 and made peace with Louis, the Church and Otto the Great in 953.

certainty.note: A march and a ducal title, never a bounded state: the pages give 'the region between the Loire and the Seine' and a few counties; every frontier is approximate.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from four pages (Breton March, Duchy of Francia, Robert the Strong, Hugh the Great). The state is the Robertian march of Neustria (861) that became the Duchy of Francia (936) and the Capetian domain (987, kingdom-of-france); rule 2 keeps it one dossier with a rename in 936. It lies inside West Francia, whose Cliopatria shapes (850-989) cover the same land: the compile must subtract it or treat it as a vassal-like tint. The URL 'Breton_March' returned the article on the Marches of Neustria, not the Carolingian Breton March (c. 778-851: Roland, Guy, Widmar, Lambert, Nominoë), which therefore has no dossier here; a gap-filler should open 'Breton-Frankish wars' or 'Marca Britannica'. Thin spots (confidence 1 or reading): the Robertians' extent between 866 and 936 (the pages give only Anjou, Maine, Autun/Nevers and Tours abbacy before Hugh the Great's 936 land); Autun and Nevers (856) are not drawn; the 911 grant of the Norman March (March page) is not drawn because the Hugh the Great page says the land ceded to the Normans in 911 was excluded; Hugh the Great's duchies of Burgundy and Aquitaine (granted by Lothair, undated; Gilbert of Burgundy died 8 April 956) are personal unions not drawn; the Duchy of Burgundy before 1003 and the Duchy of Aquitaine 896-989 need dossiers (counterparts_needing_dossiers). The Hugh the Great page gives no 943 titles and the Duchy page no 861 or 866 dates for Robert; these come from the other pages. Capitals Angers (861-885) and Paris (886-987) are bridges: no page names a seat. Wikidata id left null. Gazetteer names: regions Maine (France), Anjou, Touraine, Orleanais, Ile-de-France, Poitou all exist; 'western Anjou' is a lon/lat circle.
